description: NIGHTDRIVE asset manifest — documents the required image files, their resolution, how the engine composites them, and which slots a customisation phase can swap.
targetDisplay: 1920x1080 (source plates are 1376x768 and are only ever downscaled from there)

encoding.why: 4:2:0 chroma subsampling smeared the car's edges, and the old night plates were quantised to 0.59-0.82 bits/pixel, which is what produced the blocky night sky. scripts/validate.mjs fails the build if a plate drops below 1280x720, loses 4:4:4 chroma, or falls under 1.0 bits/pixel.

scene.description: Cool blue-peach dawn light, mist in valley, pine trees, black Challenger, headlights OFF
Full daylight, clear blue sky, mountain peaks, green valley, Challenger headlights OFF
Warm amber/orange sun near horizon, dramatic shadows, rim-lit Challenger, headlights OFF
Deep blue/purple twilight, last glow on mountain peaks, Challenger with lamps lit in the plate

headlights.description: Volumetric beam cone and wet-road spill. Emitter rings dissolved so the overlay adds glow instead of a second set of lamps.

scene.description: Dark mountain road, single moon, Challenger with lamps lit in the plate
scene.derivation: Per-channel colour grade fitted to the original night plate (~1 luminance level residual), so the shared camera pose is carried over and the crossfade does not jump. The photographic moon from assets/moon.jpg is composited in place of the original 40px moon.

scene.description: Deepest night, cold blue tones, paler moon, lamps lit in the plate
scene.derivation: Same fitted grade as night, with a cooler/dimmer moon to match the deeper sky.

sourceAssets.assets/moon.jpg: 2580x2452 lunar plate, used to build the moon composited into night and midnight.

regeneration.scripts/rebuild-assets.py: Rebuilds night and midnight from the dusk master and re-encodes every plate at 4:4:4 / q95.
regeneration.scripts/build-headlights.py: Rebuilds the beam overlay for dusk, night and midnight from the original beam plate.
regeneration.scripts/rebuild-assets.py --derived-only: Rewrites only night and midnight from the shipped dusk master, for changes to the moon composite. Skips the badge retouch (the dusk master already has it) and leaves the other four plates byte-identical, so they do not gain a JPEG generation.

knownLimitations: All six plates are 1376x768 and landscape-only. That is a true 1:1 match at 1366x768 and a slight downscale at 1080p, but 1440p and 4K displays still upscale. The precise fix is six identically composed 2560x1440 masters; no external paths are referenced because those files do not exist yet.
No portrait plates ship. The engine handles their absence correctly (contained over a blurred backdrop) but a native portrait render would look better.
No independent car layer ships, so the car cannot be swapped without re-rendering the plate.
morning/day/goldenHour use a closer, front-on camera than dusk/night/midnight. Composition is consistent within each group but the car's scale shifts across the midday-to-dusk boundary.
The plates show a muscle car, not the EV/sports-car direction named in the brief. That needs new plates rather than retouching.
The beam overlay is a generic headlight render positioned by a single CSS transform. It aligns well at the shipped 16:9 plates but was not authored against the car's exact lamp coordinates.
A ~2 px fender emblem is faintly present on the front three-quarter plates. It is not legible at any supported display size and was left alone rather than risk an inpaint artifact on the dark paint.
Weather changes the sky not at all: the plates are fixed and the Open-Meteo data only drives the temperature/icon widget.

modelBadge.method: mask-based inpaint, feathered into the grille, core pulled to a local blur
modelBadge.note: The plates carried a small '392' model badge on the grille. The brief forbids baked-in model names and logos, so it was retouched out of all six.

moonComposite.mode: screen-transmittance + windowed Mie halo (zero dark limb ring)

slots.portrait: Optional tall plate per period, preferred on a tall viewport. Absent: the landscape plate is shown contained over a blurred copy of itself.
slots.cursor: Optional transparent car layer drawn over the plate (empty today — the car is part of the photograph).
slots.focus: Car position as x% y%, used as object-position so narrow/portrait viewports crop toward the car.
